title: Electrical impedance tomography for the detection of regional respiratory flow limitation during undisturbed resting breathing
summary: The BREATHE study investigates the use of Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT) to identify regional flow limitations in the lungs during resting breathing. This method aims to complement and improve conventional lung function diagnostics, which are based on active breathing maneuvers. EIT allows real-time visualization of ventilation changes in different lung regions, enabling more accurate diagnosis and treatment planning, particularly for chronic lung diseases such as COPD. The goal is to detect obstructive changes without the need for strenuous breathing maneuvers. The study plans to recruit 125 participants, including COPD patients and healthy non-smokers.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Healthy non-smokers or a clinical/anamnestic suspicion of COPD
Exclusion criteria:
- Withdrawal of informed consent
- Contraindications for forced breathing maneuvers (e.g., acute myocardial infarction, acute fulminant pulmonary embolism, large ascending aortic aneurysm, tension pneumothorax)
- Pacemaker or other electrically active thoracic implants
- Wounds or open skin lesions in the thoracic area
- History of thoracic surgery (e.g., lung segment resection, cardiac surgery, esophagus resection)
- Asthma
- Pulmonary fibrosis
- Cystic fibrosis
- Advanced heart failure (≥ NYHA III or ACC/AHA Stage C-D)
- Lack of ability to provide informed consent
